previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis and chronic steroid-dependent asthma was admitted for weakness, shortness of breath, and abdominal pain after resuming alcohol use. He was treated for alcohol withdrawal with CIWA protocol, thiamine, and folate. His respiratory symptoms were attributed to a severe asthma exacerbation, managed with high-dose steroids, nebulizers, and oxygen, with gradual improvement. Elevated beta glucan and pulmonary nodules on CT prompted concern for PCP or fungal infection; he was started on Bactrim prophylaxis and underwent a CT-guided lung biopsy, which revealed scar tissue. An EGD showed esophageal candidiasis, treated with fluconazole. Liver imaging showed stable cirrhosis without HCC but worsening portal hypertension. He was discharged on a prednisone taper, fluconazole, Bactrim, and liver support medications, with follow-up arranged in pulmonology, hepatology, and primary care.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  ULTRASOUND ABDOMEN

INDICATION:  ___ male with epigastric pain and elevated alkaline
phosphatase.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

The liver is diffusely echogenic, with a nodular contour and a hypertrophic
left liver lobe compatible with liver cirrhosis.  Limited visualization of the
gallbladder shows a 4 mm echogenic focus an and endplate the tendon
dislocation which may represent a cholesterol polyp.  The gallbladder is not
distended.  There is no pericholecystic fluid or gallbladder wall edema.  the
common bile duct is not dilated, measuring 4 mm.  There is no perihepatic
fluid.  Moderate splenomegaly is present, with the spleen measuring 16.5 cm.

Assessment of the portal vein is limited given inability of the patient to
hold his breath and difficulty with acoustic penetration of the liver. 
Allowing for this limitation there is apparent reversal of flow in the main
portal vein and the right portal vein.  Assessment of the left portal vein is
limited.  The main, right, left hepatic arteries showed normal waveform and
peak systolic velocity.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Appearance of the liver compatible with liver cirrhosis.

2.  Reverse directionality of flow in the main and right portal vein as well
as moderate splenomegaly are consistent with portal hypertension.

3.  No evidence of cholecystitis.

EXAMINATION:  CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ male with ethanol cirrhosis presenting with severe
abdominal pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial helical MDCT images were obtained from the lung bases to the
lesser trochanters after administration of intravenous contrast. Coronal and
sagittal reformations were prepared.

DLP: 991 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  Abdominal ultrasound performed on the same date

FINDINGS: 

CT ABDOMEN:  The lung bases are clear. The visualized portions of the heart
pericardium are normal.

The liver shows a nodular contour in keeping with known history of liver
cirrhosis.  There is a 2.0 x 2.2 cm exophytic mass, originating from segment
4B and abutting the fundus of the gallbladder (series 2, image 37).  No other
focal liver lesion is identified.  There is no intrahepatic biliary duct
dilatation.  The study is very limited for assessment of the portal vein is
although there appears to be early cavernous transformation of the portal vein
and the anterior branch of the right portal vein appears diminutive and is
lost about 1 cm after its origin.  The gallbladder is unremarkable.  There is
recanalization of the umbilical vein.

There is moderate splenomegaly, with the spleen measuring 15 cm of
anteroposterior dimension.  There is extensive perisplenic varicosities, with
evidence of splenorenal shunt.  Small paraesophageal and perigastric varices
are also present.  There is no ascites.

The pancreas, adrenal glands, and kidneys are within normal limits.  There is
no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There is no free air or
abdominal wall hernia. The aorta is non aneurysmal.  The main intra-abdominal
vessels are grossly patent.

There is minimal dilatation of a single loop of small bowel in the left hemi
abdomen, a nonspecific finding.  There is no evidence of small bowel
obstruction. The colon is within normal limits.  The appendix is visualized
and is not inflamed.

CT PELVIS:  The urinary bladder is unremarkable.  The prostate is not
enlarged.  There is no pelvic wall or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  No pelvic
free fluid is identified.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: There is no lytic or blastic lesion worrisome for
malignancy.  A healing fracture is seen in the left anterior fifth rib.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Liver cirrhosis with stigmata of portal hypertension including
splenomegaly, splenic varices with a splenorenal shunting, periesophageal and
perigastric varices, recanalization of the umbilical vein.  No evidence of
ascites.

2.  Exophytic mass in segment 4B of the liver in this patient with liver
cirrhosis may represent a cirrhotic nodule versus hepatocellular carcinoma. 
Further assessment with multiphasic MR or CT is recommended.

3.  Limited study for assessment of the portal veins.  Allowing for this
limitation there is apparent early cavernous transformation of the portal vein
and diminutive portal vein branches, with loss of the anterior branch of the
right portal vein immediately after the bifurcation.  Further assessment of
the patency of the portal veins could be performed at the time of the
multiphasic MR or CT performed for evaluation of the exophytic mass.

4.  No evidence of acute abdominal or pelvic process.

5.  Healing fracture of the left anterior fifth rib.

EXAMINATION:  ___ DUP EXTEXT BIL (MAP/DVT)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with EtOH pancreatitis and EtOH withdrawal who
has asymmetric swelling in ___.  // Is there a DVT?

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed
of the lower extremity veins bilaterally.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

There is normal compressibility, flow and augmentation of bilateral common
femoral, femoral, and popliteal veins. Normal color flow is demonstrated in
the posterior tibial and peroneal veins bilaterally.

There is normal respiratory variation in the common femoral veins bilaterally.

No evidence of medial popliteal fossa (___) cyst.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of deep venous thrombosis in the either leg.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with EtOH withdrawal and pancreatitis  // Is
there a PNA?      Is there a PNA?

COMPARISON:  Prior chest radiographs since ___ most recently ___.

IMPRESSION: 

Lungs are clear.  Heart size normal.  Mediastinal and hilar silhouettes and
pleural surfaces are essentially normal.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with EtOH cirrhosis, now with mass on liver  //
Is there an HCC?

TECHNIQUE:  T1- and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen were
acquired in a 1.5 T magnet.
Intravenous contrast: Gadavist 10 cc.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___ MRCP ___.

FINDINGS: 

The liver is normal in size and nodular in contour.  There is mild hepatic
steatosis.  There are patchy confluent regions of fibrosis with increased
reticular T2 signal and delayed enhancement.  Within the region of abnormality
seen on recent CT scan within segment IVb there are several T1 hyperintense,
T2 isointense nodular areas without associated restricted diffusion and
without demonstration of arterial hyper enhancement or delayed washout within
areas of fibrosis, most consistent with regenerative nodules (series 1304
images 78 - 97).  No concerning hepatic mass is seen.  The portal vein is
patent.  There is conventional hepatic arterial anatomy.

There is trace perihepatic ascites.  The spleen is enlarged measuring 15.5 cm
in craniocaudal dimension.  There are prominent perisplenic and gastrohepatic
ligament varices.  There has been recanalization of the paraumbilical vein.

There is mild pericholecystic and retroperitoneal edema, likely on the basis
of portal hypertension.  The gallbladder is fluid filled and without evidence
of wall thickening or filling defects.

There is no abdominal lymphadenopathy.

The adrenal glands are within normal limits.

The pancreatic parenchyma is normal in signal intensity.  Pancreatic duct is
normal in caliber.  No pancreatic mass is seen.

The kidneys are normal in size and symmetrically enhancing without evidence of
hydronephrosis.  No concerning renal mass is seen.

Visualized portions of the bowel are unremarkable.

The bone marrow signal is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Cirrhosis with associated stigmata of portal hypertension including
splenomegaly, perisplenic and gastrohepatic ligament varices and
recanalization of the paraumbilical vein.
2.  No evidence of HCC.
3.  Patchy areas of confluent fibrosis with several regenerative nodules seen
within segment IVB within an area of fibrosis, corresponding to the
abnormality seen on recent CT.
4.  Mild hepatic steatosis.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Routine hepatic surveillance based on hepatic risk
factors.
